issues.description: Close message type is wrong — PR description says CloseStream, code sends Close
issues.detail: The whole point of this patch, per its own commit message and linked Deepgram docs, is to send {"type": "CloseStream"}. The code sends {"type": "Close"}. These are not the same string. If Deepgram's protocol requires CloseStream, this patch does not fix the bug it claims to fix. Either the constant is wrong or the commit message is wrong — pick one and make them match before this lands.

issues.description: Bare except Exception swallows everything including CancelledError on older Pythons
issues.detail: except Exception catches too much. If the socket is already half-closed, you'll log a warning every shutdown and pollute logs. Worse, on shutdown paths this hides real bugs behind a generic warning. Catch the specific aiohttp/connection errors you actually expect (ConnectionResetError, aiohttp.ClientError, etc.) and let the rest propagate.

issues.description: Single ws.receive() with 1s timeout is not 'wait for ack' — it's 'wait for next frame'
issues.detail: The comment claims this waits for server acknowledgment. It doesn't. ws.receive() returns whatever the next frame is — could be an audio chunk in flight, could be anything. To actually drain until the server signals close, you need a loop that reads until you see the close ack or a close frame, with the timeout bounding the whole drain. As written this is cargo-cult synchronization and the comment is a lie.

issues.description: Two patches in one — Flush is not part of the stated fix
issues.detail: Commit message says 'send CloseStream before closing.' The diff also sends Flush. That's two behavior changes. Either Flush is required (then say so in the commit message and justify it) or it isn't (then drop it). One patch, one thing. This is THREE-PATCHES territory at minimum: constant rename, Flush-on-close, drain-before-close.

issues.description: f-string in logger call instead of lazy formatting
issues.detail: logger.warning(f"...{e}") formats the string even when the log level filters it out. Use logger.warning("Error during WebSocket close sequence: %s", e). Minor, but it's the codebase convention in most Python projects and costs nothing to do right.

issues.description: Class-level constants defined on subclass but referenced via subclass name from parent scope method
issues.detail: SynthesizeStream._FLUSH_MSG is referenced inside _close_ws, which lives on a different class. That works but it's ugly — _close_ws now has a hard dependency on a sibling class's internal constants. Either move the constants to module scope or move _close_ws onto SynthesizeStream. Don't reach across class boundaries to grab a JSON string.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The most damning issue: the PR title and description say it sends CloseStream, but the code sends {"type": "Close"}. If Deepgram's API requires CloseStream (as the linked docs suggest), this patch doesn't fix what it claims to fix — verify against the actual Deepgram speak v1 protocol and reconcile the mismatch before anything else. Beyond that, the close sequence is sloppy: a bare except Exception, a single ws.receive() pretending to be an ack wait, an f-string in a logger call, and Flush quietly bolted onto a patch whose commit message only mentions Close. This is two or three patches stuffed into one. Shape it up: one patch for the protocol message (with the right name), one for the drain loop if you actually want to drain, and keep Flush separate or justify it explicitly.
